title: TurfBD — Multi-Tenant Sports Booking Platform
summary: Multi-tenant sports turf booking backend in Rust with distributed rate limiting and reliable background jobs.
description: TurfBD is a multi-tenant platform for booking sports turfs. The backend is written in Rust (Axum, SQLx, Tokio) on PostgreSQL, with Redis for distributed rate limiting and RabbitMQ for background work, and ships as Docker containers with CI/CD via GitHub Actions.
highlights: Built a custom distributed Token Bucket rate limiter using an atomic Redis Lua script
Designed a Transactional Outbox Pattern with idempotency guarantees and dead-letter queuing

### Phase 3 — Local admin panel
Split in 3 sub-steps so each can be tested alone:

**3a — Data & GitHub import**
- [x] `admin/index.html` layout + sidebar; load baseline from `../public/data/*.json`
- [x] URL parser, README (raw) + languages fetch, bytes→% conversion, error handling (404/403/network), optional token in `sessionStorage`
- [x] Project editor form with validation (slug, unique id, ≤5 highlights, URL formats); merge-on-reimport rules
- [x] Reorder (up/down) + featured toggle + delete with confirm

**3b — Notes & posts editor**
- [x] Split-pane markdown editor with live sanitized preview
- [x] Tags, date picker (defaults to today), summary field, slug auto-generation
- [x] Per-project notes CRUD and global blog CRUD

**3c — Drafts & export**
- [x] Autosave drafts to `localStorage`, "differs from live" indicator, discard/reset
- [x] Unsaved-changes warning
- [x] Export `projects.json` / `blog.json` (pretty-printed, 2-space indent, stable key order to keep git diffs small); optional File System Access write
- [x] Validate before export (block on errors)

notes.title: Why I replaced Fixed-Window with Token Bucket rate limiting
notes.summary: A look at boundary-loophole attacks and how Token Bucket eliminates them.
notes.content:
## Background

The fixed window counter resets at a hard boundary, so a client can send a full quota at the end of one window and another full quota at the start of the next.

## The fix

A Token Bucket refills continuously and allows bursts up to a capacity, with the check-and-take done atomically in a Redis Lua script.

title: ChatDistill
summary: A Chrome MV3 extension built with vanilla DOM and scoped CSS.
description: ChatDistill is a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) that transforms verbose, unstructured conversations from ChatGPT into high-signal, formatted Markdown notes and PDF summaries. Built with TypeScript, Vite, and vanilla scoped DOM rendering, it features a 2-layer extraction cascade, profile presets (Developer, Executive, Student) to guide LLM synthesis depth, and privacy-safe error telemetry.
highlights: Engineered a 2-layer extraction cascade: direct API interception bypassing virtual scrolling with DOM selector fallback
Designed profile presets enforcing prompt depth, focus, and token-efficient formatting via Gemini API
Implemented privacy-safe error telemetry with automated DOM skeleton anonymization for zero-middlemen debugging
